To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose the first differentiable panoptic segmentation model that is based on a combinatorial solver, and that our model achieves state-of-the-art performance on the COCO panoptic segmentation benchmark.

1) a fully differentiable combinatorial optimization approach is a viable solution for the panoptic segmentation task; 2) our architecture achieves state-of-the-art results on the Cityscapes and COCO panoptic segmentation datasets; 3) the panoptic segmentation problem is a challenging one, which is still far from being solved, and there is still room for improvement.

1) the panoptic quality of a segmentation network can be optimized by solving a combinatorial problem, 2) this combinatorial problem is a generalization of the asymmetric multiway cut (AMC) problem, 3) the AMC problem can be solved in a fully differentiable fashion, 4) the resulting architecture can be trained in an end-to-end fashion and achieves a state-of-the-art performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: \emph{How to learn a panoptic segmentation model that can directly maximize the panoptic quality?
two questions: (i) How do we design an architecture to produce panoptic predictions?
the following questions: (1) How do we formulate the panoptic segmentation problem as a combinatorial optimisation task?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed architecture is a fully differentiable approach for simultaneous semantic and boundary segmentation (a.k. panoptic segmentation).
this work is an interesting attempt to combine deep learning with combinatorial optimization for a specific task, but it is not yet clear how useful the resulting model is.
the proposed method is a fully differentiable approach that can solve a panoptic segmentation problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a fully differentable architecture for panoptic segmentation that can directly maximize a surrogate of PQ by backpropagatng the gradient through the combinatorial optimization.
we propose a differentiable architecture that can directly optimize the panoptic quality.
we propose a fully differentable framework for the task of panoptic segmentation that can be trained end-to-end with any off-the-shelf segmentation model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
combinatorial optimization problems can be used in a fully differentiable manner to solve challenging computer vision tasks such as panoptic segmentation.
the panoptic quality of the resulting segmentation can be significantly improved over a baseline network by solving a combinatorial problem with a few thousand variables.
combinatorial optimization is a viable and efficient way to perform panoptic segmentation, and that our formulation allows to learn a panoptic model from end to end.
